ChurchTools aus Python und Rust ansprechen

Ein Client für die gesamte ChurchTools-REST-API: typisierte Antworten, Fehler mit verständlicher Meldung, automatisches Blättern durch lange Listen.

  • 849 Endpunkte
  • 1110 Modelle
  • API-Stand ChurchTools 3.138.0 (build 32935)
Erster Aufruf Projekte ansehen Zur Referenz

Einstieg

Vom Installieren bis zum ersten Aufruf in wenigen Minuten.

Worum es geht

churchtools-rs ist ein Client für die REST-API von ChurchTools: Personen, Gruppen, Kalender, Events, Dienste, Lieder, Finanzen und alles Weitere, was die API anbietet.

Es gibt ihn für zwei Sprachen. Beide entstehen aus derselben API-Beschreibung und funktionieren gleich:

  • Python: Rückgaben sind Pydantic-Modelle mit Autovervollständigung in der IDE.
  • Rust: Rückgaben sind serde-Structs, Fehler sind ein Result.

Wähle oben rechts deine Sprache. Alle Beispiele auf dieser Seite wechseln mit.

Was du brauchst

  • Die Adresse deiner ChurchTools-Instanz, z. B. https://meinegemeinde.church.tools.
  • Ein Login-Token für alles, was nicht öffentlich ist. Das Token gehört zu einer Person in ChurchTools, und der Client sieht genau das, was diese Person sehen darf. Für Skripte lohnt sich ein eigener Benutzer mit passend eingeschränkten Rechten.

Öffentliche Daten wie öffentliche Kalender funktionieren auch ohne Token. Damit kannst du sofort loslegen.

Installation

Das Python-Paket enthält einen kompilierten Rust-Kern und wird mit maturin gebaut. In Rust bindest du die Crate churchtools-core als Abhängigkeit ein.

# im Ordner python/ des Projekts
pip install maturin
maturin develop          # baut und installiert churchtools-rs ins aktive venv
# Cargo.toml
[dependencies]
churchtools-core = { path = "../churchtools-rs/core" }

Dein erster Aufruf

Dieses Programm fragt ab, welche ChurchTools-Version eine Instanz verwendet. Es braucht kein Token und läuft gegen die öffentliche Demo-Instanz.

Danach bist du startklar. Die folgenden Beispiele zeigen nur noch den Teil, der sich ändert, und setzen einen fertigen client voraus.

import churchtools_rs as ct

client = ct.Client("https://demo.church.tools")
info = client.info.get()
print(info.site_name, info.version)
use churchtools_core::Client;

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let client = Client::new("https://demo.church.tools", None)?;
    let info = client.info().get()?;
    println!("{:?} {:?}", info.site_name, info.version);
    Ok(())
}

Ausgabe: ChuToo Church 3.138.0

Grundlagen

Die Konzepte, die für jeden Aufruf gelten. Wer sie kennt, findet sich in der ganzen Referenz zurecht.

Client und Anmeldung

Ein Client gehört zu einer Instanz und einem Token. Das Token wird als Authorization: Login <token> mitgeschickt. Du musst dich um nichts weiter kümmern.

Lege das Token nicht in den Quelltext. Am einfachsten liest du es aus den Umgebungsvariablen CT_URL und CT_TOKEN.

import churchtools_rs as ct

client = ct.Client("https://meinegemeinde.church.tools", token="DEIN_TOKEN")

# besser: CT_URL und CT_TOKEN aus der Umgebung lesen
client = ct.Client.from_env()

me = client.whoami.get()
print(f"Angemeldet als {me.first_name} {me.last_name}")
use churchtools_core::Client;

let client = Client::new("https://meinegemeinde.church.tools", Some("DEIN_TOKEN".into()))?;

// besser: CT_URL und CT_TOKEN aus der Umgebung lesen
let client = Client::from_env()?;

let me = client.whoami().get()?;
println!("Angemeldet als {:?} {:?}", me.first_name, me.last_name);

Anfragen drosseln

Für Skripte, die viele Anfragen schicken, kannst du einen Mindestabstand zwischen zwei Anfragen festlegen. So belastest du die Instanz nicht unnötig. Der Abstand gilt auch für Kopien des Clients.

Antwortet der Server mit 429 Too Many Requests, wartet der Client die verlangte Zeit (Retry-After, höchstens 60 Sekunden) und versucht es bis zu dreimal erneut. Das passiert immer, auch ohne Mindestabstand. Bei 502, 503 und 504 wiederholt er lesende und andere idempotente Anfragen (GET, PUT, DELETE) genauso; ein POST wird nicht wiederholt, weil er sonst doppelt ausgeführt werden könnte. Kommt keine Verbindung zustande, versucht er es nach einer Sekunde einmal erneut.

Für Tests gegen eine Demo-Instanz gibt es außerdem login_with_password. Es meldet sich mit Benutzername und Passwort an und holt das Login-Token der Person. In eigenen Skripten ist ein gespeichertes Token besser.

# höchstens vier Anfragen pro Sekunde
client = ct.Client.from_env(min_interval=0.25)

for person in client.persons.list():
    print(person.id, person.first_name)

# nur für Tests: mit Benutzername und Passwort anmelden
test = ct.Client("https://xyz.church.tools").login_with_password("benutzer", "passwort")
use std::time::Duration;

// höchstens vier Anfragen pro Sekunde
let client = Client::from_env()?.with_min_interval(Duration::from_millis(250));

for person in client.persons().list()? {
    println!("{} {:?}", person.id, person.first_name);
}

// nur für Tests: mit Benutzername und Passwort anmelden
let test = Client::new("https://xyz.church.tools", None)?.login_with_password("benutzer", "passwort")?;

Wie Aufrufe aufgebaut sind

Jeder Aufruf folgt dem Pfad der API. Aus jedem festen Teil des Pfads wird eine Ressource. Platzhalter wie {groupId} werden zu Argumenten:

APIPythonRust
GET /groupsclient.groups.list()client.groups().list()
GET /groups/{groupId}client.groups.get(42)client.groups().get(42)
GET /groups/{groupId}/membersclient.groups.members.list(42)client.groups().members().list(42)

Der Methodenname richtet sich nach der HTTP-Methode:

HTTPMethodebedeutet
GETlist / getmehrere lesen / eins lesen
POSTcreateneu anlegen
PUTupdateersetzen oder setzen
PATCHpatcheinzelne Felder ändern
DELETEdeletelöschen

Aktionen behalten ihren Namen, z. B. client.persons.invite(7) für POST /persons/{personId}/invite.

group = client.groups.get(42)
print(group.name)

for member in client.groups.members.list(42):
    print(member.person.title)
let group = client.groups().get(42)?;
println!("{}", group.name);

for member in client.groups().members().list(42)? {
    println!("{}", member.person.title);
}

Parameter übergeben

Es gibt drei Arten von Parametern:

  • Pfad: Platzhalter im Pfad. Sie stehen vorne und haben keinen Namen.
  • Query: Filter und Optionen wie from, to, limit. In Python sind das Schlüsselwort-Argumente. In Rust gibt es dafür eine …Query-Struktur. Sind alle Filter optional, hat die Methode zwei Varianten: list() ohne Filter und list_with(&query) mit Filtern. ..Default::default() füllt alles, was du nicht setzt.
  • Body: Daten zum Anlegen oder Ändern. In Python sind es ebenfalls Schlüsselwort-Argumente, in Rust ein Modell, das du am einfachsten aus JSON erzeugst.

Die Namen sind in Python im üblichen snake_case geschrieben (first_name statt firstName). Wo ein Name ein Python-Schlüsselwort ist, kommt ein Unterstrich dazu: from_.

import datetime as dt

persons = client.persons.list(last_name="Müller", is_archived=False)

events = client.events.list(from_=dt.date(2026, 11, 1), to=dt.date(2026, 11, 30))

client.persons.patch(7, city="Esslingen", zip="73728")
let query = GetPersonsQuery {
    last_name: Some("Müller".into()),
    is_archived: Some(false),
    ..Default::default()
};
let persons = client.persons().list_with(&query)?;

let query = GetEventsQuery {
    from: Some("2026-11-01".parse()?),
    to: Some("2026-11-30".parse()?),
    ..Default::default()
};
let events = client.events().list_with(&query)?;

let body: models::PatchPersonsIdBody = serde_json::from_value(serde_json::json!({
    "city": "Esslingen",
    "zip": "73728"
}))?;
client.persons().patch(7, &body)?;

Rückgabewerte und Modelle

Antworten kommen als typisierte Objekte zurück. Die Felder heißen wie in der API, nur in snake_case.

Jede ChurchTools-Instanz kann eigene Datenbankfelder haben, die in keiner Beschreibung stehen. Diese Felder gehen nicht verloren: In Python liegen sie in model_extra, in Rust im Feld extra.

Willst du ein Objekt weitergeben oder speichern, wandelst du es in ein Dict oder JSON um.

person = client.persons.get(7)
print(person.first_name, person.birthday)

# eigene Felder der Instanz
print(person.model_extra)

# als dict / JSON (mit den Feldnamen der API)
data = person.model_dump(exclude_none=True)
text = person.model_dump_json()
let person = client.persons().get(7)?;
println!("{:?} {:?}", person.first_name, person.birthday);

// eigene Felder der Instanz
println!("{:?}", person.extra);

// als JSON (mit den Feldnamen der API)
let text = serde_json::to_string(&person)?;

Listen und Seiten

Große Listen liefert ChurchTools seitenweise. Der Client blättert für dich:

  • In Python bekommst du einen Paginator. Er lädt die nächste Seite erst, wenn du sie brauchst. Brichst du die Schleife ab, werden keine weiteren Seiten geladen. first() holt nur das erste Element, to_list() alles.
  • In Rust bekommst du gleich einen Vec mit allen Einträgen.

Mit limit bestimmst du, wie viele Einträge pro Seite geladen werden (höchstens 100).

Die Seiten werden nacheinander abgerufen. Ändert sich die Liste währenddessen, etwa weil jemand eine Person anlegt oder löscht, kann ein Eintrag doppelt vorkommen oder fehlen. Für Abgleiche lohnt es sich deshalb, nach id zu deduplizieren. Eine leere Seite beendet das Blättern, auch wenn der Server mehr Seiten ankündigt.

Der Client ist synchron. In Rust darfst du ihn nicht direkt in async-Code (Tokio) aufrufen, sondern nur über tokio::task::spawn_blocking.

for person in client.persons.list(limit=100):
    print(person.last_name)
    if person.last_name == "Zimmermann":
        break               # weitere Seiten werden nicht mehr geladen

first = client.groups.list().first()
all_groups = client.groups.list().to_list()
let query = GetPersonsQuery { limit: Some(100), ..Default::default() };
for person in client.persons().list_with(&query)? {
    println!("{:?}", person.last_name);
}

Datum und Uhrzeit

Datumswerte (Geburtstage, ganztägige Termine) sind reine Kalenderdaten. Zeitpunkte kommen immer in UTC und mit Zeitzone. Für die Anzeige rechnest du sie in die lokale Zeit um.

Termine können beides sein: Ganztägige Termine haben nur ein Datum, alle anderen einen Zeitpunkt.

import datetime as dt
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

berlin = ZoneInfo("Europe/Berlin")
event = client.events.get(42)
print(event.start_date.astimezone(berlin))   # 2026-11-01 10:00:00+01:00

# date | datetime: erst prüfen, was es ist
appointment = client.calendars.appointments.get_occurrence(42, dt.date(2026, 11, 1))
start = appointment.appointment.calculated.start_date
if isinstance(start, dt.datetime):
    print("um", start.astimezone(berlin).strftime("%H:%M"))
else:
    print("ganztägig am", start)
use churchtools_core::chrono::Local;

let event = client.events().get(42)?;
println!("{}", event.start_date.with_timezone(&Local));

// DateOrDateTime: erst prüfen, was es ist
let appointment = client.calendars().appointments()
    .get_occurrence(42, "2026-11-01")?;
match appointment.appointment.calculated.start_date {
    DateOrDateTime::DateTime(t) => println!("um {}", t.with_timezone(&Local).format("%H:%M")),
    DateOrDateTime::Date(d) => println!("ganztägig am {d}"),
}

Fehler behandeln

Antwortet ChurchTools mit einem Fehler, bekommst du die Meldung des Servers, auf Wunsch auch in der übersetzten Fassung (translated_message). In Python gibt es für die häufigsten Statuscodes eigene Ausnahmen, siehe die Fehlerübersicht. In Rust prüfst du den status.

try:
    person = client.persons.get(999999)
except ct.NotFound:
    print("Diese Person gibt es nicht.")
except ct.Unauthorized:
    print("Token fehlt oder ist abgelaufen.")
except ct.ApiError as e:
    print(e.status, e.translated_message)
use churchtools_core::Error;

match client.persons().get(999999) {
    Ok(person) => println!("{:?}", person.first_name),
    Err(Error::Api(e)) if e.status == 404 => println!("Diese Person gibt es nicht."),
    Err(Error::Api(e)) => println!("{} {:?}", e.status, e.translated_message),
    Err(e) => return Err(e.into()),
}

Felder weglassen oder leeren

Beim Ändern macht es einen Unterschied, ob ein Feld fehlt oder leer ist:

  • Weggelassen: Das Feld bleibt, wie es ist. In Python ist das der Standard (UNSET), in Rust lässt du den Schlüssel im JSON weg.
  • **None / null**: Das Feld wird geleert.

Felder, die der Client nicht kennt (z. B. eigene DB-Felder), übergibst du in Python mit extra_body.

# nur die Stadt ändern, alles andere bleibt
client.persons.patch(7, city="Esslingen")

# Geburtstag löschen
client.persons.patch(7, birthday=None)

# eigenes Datenbankfeld setzen
client.persons.patch(7, extra_body={"konfession": "evangelisch"})
let body: models::PatchPersonsIdBody = serde_json::from_value(serde_json::json!({
    "birthday": null,
    "konfession": "evangelisch"
}))?;
client.persons().patch(7, &body)?;

Projekte

Kleine, vollständige Aufgaben aus dem Gemeindealltag. Jedes Projekt verbindet mehrere Aufrufe.

Monatsplan aus öffentlichen Kalendern

Ziel: alle Termine eines Monats aus allen öffentlichen Kalendern, sortiert und in Ortszeit.

  1. Kalender laden und ihre IDs sammeln.
  2. Die Termine aller Kalender in einem Aufruf holen.
  3. Ganztägige Termine und Termine mit Uhrzeit unterschiedlich ausgeben.

Das funktioniert ohne Token, solange die Kalender öffentlich sind.

import datetime as dt
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

berlin = ZoneInfo("Europe/Berlin")
calendars = client.calendars.list()

termine = client.calendars.appointments.list(
    calendar_ids=[c.id for c in calendars],
    from_=dt.date(2026, 11, 1),
    to=dt.date(2026, 11, 30),
)
for termin in termine:
    start = termin.appointment.calculated.start_date
    if isinstance(start, dt.datetime):
        wann = start.astimezone(berlin).strftime("%d.%m. %H:%M")
    else:
        wann = start.strftime("%d.%m.") + " ganztags"
    print(wann, termin.appointment.base.title)
use churchtools_core::chrono::Local;

let calendars = client.calendars().list()?;
let query = GetCalendarsAppointmentsQuery {
    calendar_ids: Some(calendars.iter().map(|c| c.id).collect()),
    from: Some("2026-11-01".parse()?),
    to: Some("2026-11-30".parse()?),
    ..Default::default()
};
for termin in client.calendars().appointments().list(&query)? {
    let wann = match termin.appointment.calculated.start_date {
        DateOrDateTime::DateTime(t) => t.with_timezone(&Local).format("%d.%m. %H:%M").to_string(),
        DateOrDateTime::Date(d) => format!("{} ganztags", d.format("%d.%m.")),
    };
    println!("{wann} {}", termin.appointment.base.title);
}

Dienstplan für den Gottesdienst

Ziel: für jedes Event im Monat anzeigen, wer welchen Dienst übernimmt und welche Dienste noch offen sind.

  1. Die Liste der Dienste laden, um Dienst-IDs in Namen zu übersetzen.
  2. Events mit include="event_services" laden. Dann hängen die Dienste direkt am Event.
  3. Pro Dienst die eingetragene Person ausgeben oder „offen“.

Dafür braucht der Token-Benutzer Leserechte in der Dienstplanung.

import datetime as dt

dienste = {s.id: s.name for s in client.services.list()}

for event in client.events.list(
    from_=dt.date(2026, 11, 1),
    to=dt.date(2026, 11, 30),
    include="event_services",
):
    print(f"{event.start_date:%d.%m.} {event.name}")
    for eintrag in event.event_services or []:
        wer = eintrag.person.title if eintrag.person else "offen"
        print(f"    {dienste.get(eintrag.service_id, '?')}: {wer}")
use std::collections::HashMap;

let dienste: HashMap<i64, String> =
    client.services().list()?.into_iter().map(|s| (s.id, s.name)).collect();

let query = GetEventsQuery {
    from: Some("2026-11-01".parse()?),
    to: Some("2026-11-30".parse()?),
    include: Some("event_services".into()),
    ..Default::default()
};
for event in client.events().list_with(&query)? {
    println!("{} {}", event.start_date.format("%d.%m."), event.name);
    for eintrag in event.event_services.unwrap_or_default() {
        let wer = eintrag.person.map(|p| p.title).unwrap_or("offen".into());
        let dienst = dienste.get(&eintrag.service_id).map_or("?", |s| s.as_str());
        println!("    {dienst}: {wer}");
    }
}

Geburtstagsliste der Woche

Ziel: alle Geburtstage der nächsten sieben Tage, z. B. für die Mitteilungen im Gottesdienst.

ChurchTools hat dafür einen eigenen Endpunkt. Er liefert das Datum, das neue Alter und die Person.

import datetime as dt

heute = dt.date.today()
for eintrag in client.persons.list_birthdays(
    start_date=heute,
    end_date=heute + dt.timedelta(days=7),
):
    if eintrag.person:
        print(f"{eintrag.anniversary:%d.%m.}  {eintrag.person.title} wird {eintrag.age}")
use churchtools_core::chrono::{Days, Local};

let heute = Local::now().date_naive();
let query = GetPersonsBirthdaysQuery {
    start_date: Some(heute),
    end_date: heute.checked_add_days(Days::new(7)),
    ..Default::default()
};
for eintrag in client.persons().list_birthdays_with(&query)? {
    if let (Some(person), Some(tag)) = (eintrag.person, eintrag.anniversary) {
        println!("{}  {} wird {}", tag.format("%d.%m."), person.title, eintrag.age);
    }
}

Gruppenmitglieder als CSV-Datei

Ziel: die Mitglieder einer Gruppe als Tabelle, die sich in Excel oder LibreOffice öffnen lässt.

Die Mitgliederliste enthält die Person, den Status (active, requested, waiting, …) und das Eintrittsdatum. Das Semikolon als Trennzeichen erkennt Excel in deutscher Einstellung direkt.

import csv

with open("mitglieder.csv", "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
    writer = csv.writer(f, delimiter=";")
    writer.writerow(["Name", "Status", "Mitglied seit"])
    for member in client.groups.members.list(42):
        writer.writerow([member.person.title, member.group_member_status, member.member_start_date or ""])
let mut csv = String::from("Name;Status;Mitglied seit\n");
for member in client.groups().members().list(42)? {
    let seit = member.member_start_date.map(|d| d.to_string()).unwrap_or_default();
    csv += &format!("{};{};{}\n", member.person.title, member.group_member_status, seit);
}
std::fs::write("mitglieder.csv", csv)?;

Neue Person anlegen und in eine Gruppe aufnehmen

Ziel: eine Anmeldung aus einem Formular übernehmen: Person anlegen und direkt einer Gruppe zuordnen.

  1. Person mit Abteilung (department_ids) und Namen anlegen. Die Abteilung ist Pflicht.
  2. Mit der neuen ID die Mitgliedschaft in der Gruppe setzen.

ChurchTools prüft beim Anlegen auf Dubletten. Findet es eine ähnliche Person, antwortet es mit einem Fehler. force=True legt die Person trotzdem an.

person = client.persons.create(
    department_ids=[1],
    first_name="Ben",
    last_name="Beispiel",
    email="ben@example.org",
)
client.groups.members.update(42, person.id, group_member_status="active")
print(f"{person.first_name} angelegt (ID {person.id}) und Gruppe 42 zugeordnet")
let body: models::PostPersonsBody = serde_json::from_value(serde_json::json!({
    "departmentIds": [1],
    "firstName": "Ben",
    "lastName": "Beispiel",
    "email": "ben@example.org"
}))?;
let person = client.persons().create(&body)?;

let membership: models::MembershipCreate =
    serde_json::from_value(serde_json::json!({ "groupMemberStatus": "active" }))?;
client.groups().members().update(42, person.id, &membership)?;
println!("{:?} angelegt (ID {})", person.first_name, person.id);

Referenz

Alle Endpunkte nach Bereichen, jeweils mit Aufruf, Parametern, Rückgabe und einem Beispiel. Beschreibungen stammen aus der offiziellen API-Beschreibung und sind englisch.

Keine Treffer. Suche nach einem Pfadteil wie members oder einem Methodennamen wie list_birthdays.

POST/externallogins*

client.externallogins.create()client.externallogins().create()

Create an external login provider

Creates an OAuth, OpenID Connect or SAML provider configuration. Requires "churchcore administer settings" permission; SAML additionally requires the SAML settings feature flag. Logo discovery may contact the provider while saving. Only one provider can be primary.

13 Parameter anzeigen
ParameterTypOrtPflichtBeschreibung
config"config"Union[ExternalLoginOAuthConfig, ExternalLoginOidcConfig, ExternalLoginSamlConfig]serde_json::ValueBodyja
create_new_person"createNewPerson"boolBodyjaWhether the login flow may create a ChurchTools person when no local identity mapping exists.
has_registration"hasRegistration"boolBodyjaWhether the external provider offers a registration flow; support depends on the protocol handler.
is_visible"isVisible"boolBody
matching_mode"matchingMode"strStringBodyDetermines how an authenticated external identity without an existing person mapping is handled.
name"name"strStringBodyjaDisplay name shown for this provider.
new_person_campus_id"newPersonCampusId"Optional[int]Option<i64>BodyjaDefault campus ID for newly created people.
new_person_department_id"newPersonDepartmentId"Optional[int]Option<i64>BodyjaDefault department ID for newly created people.
new_person_status_id"newPersonStatusId"Optional[int]Option<i64>BodyjaDefault person status ID for newly created people.
primary_login"primaryLogin"boolBody
subtitle"subtitle"Optional[str]Option<String>BodySecondary text on the login choice.
type_"type"strStringBodyjaConfigured login protocol.
update_data_on_login"updateDataOnLogin"boolBodyjaWhether existing person data is updated from provider data after successful matching.

    name="Organization login",
    new_person_campus_id=42,

POST/externallogins/oidc/backchannel-logout*

client.externallogins.oidc.backchannel_logout()client.externallogins().oidc().backchannel_logout()

Receive an OIDC back-channel logout

Accepts an OIDC Back-Channel Logout token signed by a configured provider. No browser session, CSRF token or API authentication is required. Issuer, audience, signature, lifetime, event and session/subject claims are checked. Matching local OIDC sessions are rejected on their next request. Repeated valid tokens and tokens without a matching local session succeed. Local password sessions remain unaffected. Responses have Cache-Control: no-store.

Rückgabe None()

client.externallogins.oidc.backchannel_logout()
client.externallogins().oidc().backchannel_logout()?;

GET/externallogins/{externalLoginId}/saml/login*

client.externallogins.saml.get_login()client.externallogins().saml().get_login()mit Filtern: .get_login_with(&GetExternalloginsExternalLoginIdSamlLoginQuery)

Start a SAML browser login

Starts the browser-based SAML login for a visible SAML external-login provider. Redirects to the configured identity provider with a SAML authentication request and an opaque RelayState. An optional post-login redirect is saved in the browser session, so the callback must retain that session. Only absolute URLs on this installation’s origin and within its base path are accepted; invalid redirect values are ignored. Missing, hidden or invalid providers and other setup failures produce a localized 404 response. No login or JSON access token is returned by this endpoint itself.

ParameterTypOrtPflichtBeschreibung
external_login_idintimpl DisplayPfadja
redirectstrStringQueryAbsolute same-origin destination after successful login.

Rückgabe None()

client.externallogins.saml.get_login(7)
client.externallogins().saml().get_login(7)?;

GET/externallogins/{externalLoginId}/saml/metadata

client.externallogins.saml.get_metadata()client.externallogins().saml().get_metadata()

Get SAML service-provider metadata

Returns the XML metadata that an identity-provider administrator uses to configure ChurchTools as a SAML service provider. The entity ID, assertion-consumer URL and logout URL refer to this external-login provider. This endpoint is public and also works for a hidden provider, allowing setup before enabling login. Any provider/configuration/metadata-generation failure is returned as 404 with localized text, not a JSON error envelope.

ParameterTypOrtPflichtBeschreibung
external_login_idintimpl DisplayPfadja

Rückgabe bytes (text/xml)Vec<u8> (text/xml)

with open("ergebnis.bin", "wb") as f:
    f.write(data)
let data = client.externallogins().saml().get_metadata(7)?;
std::fs::write("ergebnis.bin", &data)?;

POST/login*

client.login.create()client.login().create()

Start password-based login

Verifies a username/email and password, using configured LDAP authentication before local credentials. The configured default-login policy is enforced. HTTP 200 may mean login succeeded or that a second step is required; inspect data.status. With totp, submit the code and personId to POST /login/totp. With twoFactorSetup, initialize and activate two-factor setup before login is completed. Preserve cookies across all steps. rememberMe controls persistent browser login. Invalid credentials and locked accounts return 400, not 401. Failed local attempts increment account counters. All login steps share the configured login rate limit.

Get or create a persistent login token

Verifies username/email and password and returns the person’s existing persistent login token, creating one only if none exists. No browser login is completed by this operation. The configured default-login policy applies. Accounts with activated two-factor authentication are rejected with 400. Token retrieval is blocked during non-support simulation. The returned credential has no expiry field and remains independent of logout. Failed credential checks can increment local account error counters. This route shares the configured login rate limit with the other login steps.

POST/login/totp*

client.login.totp()client.login().totp()

Complete login with an authenticator code

Verifies the authenticator code for the person bound to the pending password-verified session. Retain the same session cookie from POST /login; this operation does not use ordinary API authentication to select a person. On success the code is temporarily blacklisted, login is completed and the pending session is removed. A pending external-account link is completed instead when that context exists. If two-factor authentication was disabled or its secret disappeared after the password step, the legacy normal-login branch returns success without redirectTo and without completing login; clients should restart the login flow. Invalid or reused codes, missing pending session and person mismatch return 400. Shares the login rate limit.

ParameterTypOrtPflichtBeschreibung
code"code"strStringBodyjaSix-digit current authenticator code.
person_id"personId"inti64BodyjaPerson ID from the password step; must match the pending two-factor session.

print(login.redirect_to)

    "personId": 42
}))?;

println!("{:?}", login.redirect_to);

POST/login/twofactor/setup*

client.login.twofactor.setup.create()client.login().twofactor().setup().create()

Initialize required authenticator setup

Starts authenticator enrollment for the person in a pending twoFactorSetup login session. Use the same cookies as the password step. Creates and stores a new secret and sets the enabled flag to false. Returns the secret and its QR-code image as a data URI. Repeating this request replaces the previous secret and invalidates its QR code, so do not use it as a read-only setup-status request. Submit a code generated from this secret to POST /login/twofactor/setup/activate. A missing or unsuitable pending session returns 400. Shares the login rate limit.

Rückgabe TwoFactorSetupSecret

result = client.login.twofactor.setup.create()
print(result.qrcode)

POST/login/twofactor/setup/activate*

client.login.twofactor.setup.activate()client.login().twofactor().setup().activate()

Activate authenticator and complete required setup

Verifies a code from the secret initialized through POST /login/twofactor/setup in the same pending login session. The session identifies the person. On success, blacklists the code, enables two-factor authentication, completes browser login using the original rememberMe choice, and clears the pending session. The response includes a navigation target from that session. Invalid/reused codes, missing secret or missing setup session return 400. Activation is saved before browser login finishes, so a later failure can leave two-factor authentication enabled. This endpoint is not an idempotent status-setting operation; after success the pending session is gone. Shares the login rate limit.

ParameterTypOrtPflichtBeschreibung
code"code"strStringBodyjaSix-digit current authenticator code.

Rückgabe PostLoginTwofactorSetupActivateData

}))?;

println!("{}", setup.redirect_to);

client.reset_password.create()client.reset_password().create()

Request password reset

Requests password-reset emails for active, non-archived accounts matching the stored email address or login name. More than one account can match. The account must already have a password, a previous login or a stored invitation login token. Eligible accounts receive a reset link valid for two weeks. The response always contains a generic translated information message, including when no account matches; it does not reveal which accounts exist or confirm delivery. This public endpoint is rate-limited (normally 20 requests per 60 seconds; configurable through ratelimit.login). Opening a valid reset link creates a password-reset session; submit the new password through PUT /persons/{personId}/password.

POST/labels*

client.labels.create()client.labels().create()

Create an address-label PDF

Generates and stores a PDF of address labels, returning an absolute download URL. Labels use the configured German address formatter and one of three A4 layouts. Only visible selected persons are included; individual printable fields are checked against security levels. Incomplete addresses are still included. With combineSpouses=true, selected visible spouses may share a label even when their addresses differ; the first spouse with a complete address is preferred. Birthday sorting forces separate labels. PDF files are scheduled to expire after one day. The generation handler checks person visibility but has no explicit create print labels permission check; the labels file-download handler checks that permission. Input is currently read without the shared request validator, so malformed input can cause server errors.

ParameterTypOrtPflichtBeschreibung
combine_spouses"combineSpouses"boolBodyCombine selected visible spouses linked by relationship type 2 into one label.
person_ids"personIds"Union[List[int], str, int]serde_json::ValueBodyjaSelected person IDs. Prefer an array of integers; legacy comma-separated strings and a single integer are also accepted.
sortpolicy"sortpolicy"strStringBodyname sorts by surname/given name; postal by country/postal code/street/name; birthday by month/day/year/name.
type_"type"strStringBodyjaA4 sheet layout: Avery3475 has 24 labels (70×36 mm), Herma4425 has 10 (105×57 mm), Herma4677 has 21 (63.5×38.1 mm).

Rückgabe PostLabelsData

        42
    ],
    "type": "AveryLabels3475"
}))?;

println!("{}", result.pdf);

These counts do not take sortpolicy or layout into account; birthday PDF sorting always uses separate labels. Stored field completeness is checked before any printable-field security filtering.

GET/persons/birthdays

client.persons.list_birthdays()client.persons().list_birthdays()mit Filtern: .list_birthdays_with(&GetPersonsBirthdaysQuery)seitenweise

Fetch Birthdays

This endpoint returns birthdays within a specific time interval. The returned objects are ordered by MONTH-DAY, where the first birthday in the list is the one next from the start date. The API also returns the age of the birthday. That age is calculated based on the date interval. That means, it is not the current age and also not the next birthday, but the age which the person had/will have at the end of the given date interval. There are two ways to utilize this endpoint: 1. With a fixed date interval (start_date, end_date). This interval must not be larger than one year. 2. With a start_date and a direction field. This combination also accepts a page and limit parameter (both with suitable defaults) to paginate through the results.

client.persons.create()client.persons().create()mit Filtern: .create_with(&PostPersonsQuery)

Create new person

Creates a person using only fields the current user may write. Before calling this endpoint, retrieve valid statusId, campusId, and departmentIds values from GET /person/masterdata. Read GET /config to determine whether privacy_policy_fields_mandatory is enabled. If it is enabled, provide all three privacy agreement fields. privacyPolicyAgreementTypeId describes how the agreement was obtained, while privacyPolicyAgreementWhoId describes who gave it; these are independent facts and must not be inferred from each other. The without_privacy_policy_agreement parameter is only effective when privacy_policy_fields_mandatory_api is disabled and must not be used without first verifying that setting. If a duplicate person is found, repeat the request with force only after intentionally deciding to create the duplicate.

PUT/persons/{personId}/password*

client.persons.update_password()client.persons().update_password()

Change the password for the active account

Changes the password for the account in the password-reset session, or otherwise the currently signed-in account. The personId path value is currently ignored and does not select the target account. A reset session takes precedence over a signed-in session; in that case oldPassword must be an empty string. Without a reset session, oldPassword must match the current password (or be empty if none exists). The new password must meet the installation’s minimum_password_length (default 8), contain ASCII upper- and lowercase letters and a digit, and exclude the person’s first name, last name and nickname case-insensitively. A successful change normally invalidates all sessions and persistent login tokens and signs out the affected current user. Initial setup from no password or the default admin password retains sessions unless using a reset session. Ordinary user simulation is forbidden; support-user simulation is exempt.

PUT/persons/{personId}/privacypolicy

client.persons.update_privacypolicy()client.persons().update_privacypolicy()

Record privacy consent

Records consent for the selected person and optionally their children. The consent banner must be enabled. The requester must be the person themselves at age 16 or above, a super administrator, or a parent authorized through relationship type 1. For own consent, a missing birthday must be supplied and the controller separately checks the age; a request can return 204 without recording own consent when that check does not pass. Children are checked against parent/child relationship type 1, missing prior consent and age below 16. If any child marked accepted is processed, 200 returns per-child outcomes, including errors or not allowed. Otherwise 204 has no body. The flow is not atomic; own consent or birthdays may already have changed when a later step fails. Unlike GET and DELETE, the acceptance policy has no explicit simulation prohibition.

own_accepted"ownAccepted"boolBodyjaWhether to process consent for the URL person.
persons"persons"List[PersonPrivacyPolicyChildUpdate]Vec<PersonPrivacyPolicyChildUpdate>BodyjaChild selections; use an empty array when not processing children.
type_id"typeId"inti64BodyjaConsent-type catalog ID used for own consent; typically the typeId from GET.
who_id"whoId"inti64BodyjaConsent-giver catalog ID used for own consent; typically the whoId from GET.

Create or update new device for person

Creates or refreshes the registration identified by personId/deviceId and returns the person’s complete device list. Requires access to update the person’s settings: the person themselves, a super administrator, or someone with administer persons permission. type is required on every call. Expiration is extended by three months, or one day during simulation. Omitted pushId becomes deviceId; empty pushId preserves the previous token; null clears it. Omitted appVersion clears the previous version. Other registrations of the same person with the same non-null push token are removed. Saving is transactional. When chat is active, a supplied appVersion outside simulation also sets the person’s hasMatrixUser setting.

Undo last service request action

Reverts the last acceptance or decline to an outstanding request. Only the assigned person may do this. The legacy history must identify this as the last action and its timestamp must be within the 10-minute undo window; otherwise 400 is returned. For a decline, use the original declined request ID, not the new unassigned record returned by the decline operation. The automatically created empty record is removed when undoing a decline. Returns the legacy response shape ServiceRequestUndoResult.

Initialize an authenticator for the current person

Verifies the current person’s username/email and password, then stores a new TOTP secret and sets twoFactorEnabled to false. Only the current person can initialize their own authenticator. Repeating this call replaces the previous secret and disables an already active authenticator. Keep the returned secret or QR code for enrollment, verify a generated code through POST /twofactor/totp, then call PUT on this path to activate. This step does not complete activation.

Sets twoFactorEnabled to true and refreshes person session data. Only the current person may activate their own authenticator. A stored secret from initialization is required; otherwise 400 is returned. No request body is consumed. Clients should first verify an authenticator code with POST /twofactor/totp; this activation handler itself checks only that a secret exists, not that a code was previously verified. Existing login tokens and other sessions are not revoked.

client.twofactor.totp()client.twofactor().totp()

Verify an authenticator code during enrollment

Checks a code against the stored authenticator secret for the current person. Only the current person may verify their own secret. Initialization must have completed first. A successful call returns status=success and records the code as used; it does not enable two-factor authentication. Call PUT /persons/{personId}/settings/twofactor separately to activate. Missing secrets, invalid codes and codes already recorded as used produce 400. Keep the code as a string to preserve leading zeroes.

GET/group/memberstatus

client.group.list_memberstatus()client.group().list_memberstatus()

Get all group member statuses

Returns the fixed membership-status values with their names translated into the current language. A status describes a person's membership state in a group; their role (for example leader or participant) is a separate property. active means an active membership, requested a membership awaiting confirmation, waiting a place on the waiting list, and to_delete a membership pending removal. to_delete is still a stored membership state, not an already deleted record. These values are shared across group types. Use id in API requests and name for display. Requires authentication. This endpoint takes no parameters and returns a plain array, without a data wrapper or meta object. It lists possible statuses, not the transitions that a particular user may perform for a particular membership.

for memberstatu in client.group.list_memberstatus():
    print(memberstatu.name)

    println!("{}", memberstatu.name);
}

Get all age ranges

Returns all age ranges configured in this ChurchTools installation. An age range describes intended participant ages, such as ages 3 to 5. Groups can reference several ranges through information.ageGroupIds. These configured ranges are independent of the calculated ages of current members. Requires authentication, but no master-data editing permission. There are no filter or pagination parameters. Results are ordered by sortKey ascending and then by the stored name ascending; meta.count is the number of returned records. IDs and labels are installation-specific; discover them before assigning them to groups.

POST/group/agegroups

client.group.agegroups.create()client.group().agegroups().create()

Create age range

Creates a age range as shared master data. An age range describes intended participant ages, such as ages 3 to 5. Groups can reference several ranges through information.ageGroupIds. These configured ranges are independent of the calculated ages of current members. Requires the churchgroup permission "edit masterdata". Supply name, sortKey, start and end. Age boundaries are expressed in years. The name is trimmed. The endpoint validates integer boundaries but does not check that start is less than or equal to end; send a meaningful range. Returns the created record with its generated ID and translated display name. Creating this record does not create or assign any groups.

start"start"inti64BodyjaLower age boundary in years, inclusive.

GET/group/grouptypes

client.group.grouptypes.list()client.group().grouptypes().list()

Get all group types

Returns all group types configured in this ChurchTools installation. Group types are shared configuration records (master data), for example "Small group" or "Ministry team". A group is a concrete collection of people, such as "Tuesday evening small group", and references one type through information.groupTypeId. Each type defines common settings and has its own membership roles, such as leader or participant. Use GET /group/roles to retrieve role definitions and match their groupTypeId to the type's id. Use GET /groups to retrieve actual groups; this endpoint does not return groups or their members. Requires authentication. No master-data editing permission is required. The response is not paginated and accepts no filters. Results are ordered by sortKey ascending, then by the stored name ascending. meta.count is the number of group types returned. IDs and names are installation-specific; integrations should discover them instead of assuming fixed values.

GET/group/roles

Get roles

Returns membership-role definitions shared by groups of a given group type. For example, a small-group type may define leader, co-leader and participant roles. Use group_type_id to select one type; omitting it returns roles for all types. A type with no matching roles returns an empty data array. The default standard format returns full Role objects. domainObject returns compact display references with a string domainIdentifier instead of the full role fields. Use GET /groups/{groupId}/roles for the settings of these roles in a specific group. Requires authentication, but no master-data editing permission. The list is not paginated; meta.count is the number of returned roles. Without a filter, results are sorted by sortKey and name ascending. With group_type_id, they are sorted by type and sortKey ascending.

group_type_idinti64QueryID of the group type whose role definitions to return.

client.groups.list_posts()client.groups().list_posts()mit Filtern: .list_posts_with(&GetGroupsGroupIdPostsQuery)seitenweise

Get visible posts of a group

Returns published, unexpired and unbanned local posts visible to the current user in this group. Anonymous access is supported and limited by public group and post visibility. Posts must be enabled for both the group and its group type. Group-internal posts require membership; other posts follow group visibility. A missing or inaccessible group returns an empty list. Explicitly selecting a group includes it even when the user has hidden the group from their feed; hidden posts and hidden authors remain excluded. External instances are not queried. Results are ordered by publishedDate and GUID descending. For the next batch, pass the last post’s publishedDate as before and its guid as last_post_identifier. page is ignored; pagination.current stays 1, and total/lastPage describe the remaining cursor-filtered results rather than the complete feed.

client.groups.update_grouphomepage()client.groups().update_grouphomepage()

Create or update a group’s homepage configuration

Creates the homepage configuration if none exists, otherwise updates it. Requires permission to edit the parent group’s basic settings. Existing URL hashes are preserved; newly created pages receive a random hash. Supply all five enabled/display flags. Omitted header modes and custom text preserve existing values; omitted layout, ordering, collapse and depth settings reset to defaults, and omitted filters disables all filters. POST/groups/{groupId}/duplicate

client.groups.duplicate()client.groups().duplicate()mit Filtern: .duplicate_with(&PostGroupsIdDuplicateQuery)

Duplicate a group with selected related data

Creates a pending group with a new ID, GUID and name. Requires permission to create a group with the source group’s type, campus and parent groups. The copy includes both parent and child hierarchy links, tags, membership field definitions, role settings, addresses and the group image. Memberships, role permissions and membership routines are copied only when their flags are enabled. Meetings and the appointment link are cleared. An existing group homepage is cloned with a new URL hash. Supply newName and optional flags in the query or JSON body; query values take precedence. The returned group is not enriched with all copied related data.

Announces a group to potential new members through push notifications. Requires permission to edit the group’s basic settings. GET/groups/{groupId}/meetings

client.groups.meetings.list()client.groups().meetings().list()mit Filtern: .list_with(&GetGroupsIdMeetingsQuery)seitenweise

Get meetings for a group

Returns meetings and attendance statistics for a group. Requires authentication, permission to view the group and permission to manage its meetings.

Without direction, returns all meetings with startDate >= from and startDate < to, ordered oldest first. page and limit do not restrict this date-range mode. Defaults are yesterday at midnight through midnight 30 days after today, in the application timezone.

With direction=forward, returns meetings strictly after from, oldest first. With direction=backward, returns meetings strictly before from, newest first. In this mode to is ignored, and page/limit select a page. The response has no pagination object or total page count.

meta.count is the number returned; meta.statistics covers all meetings of the group. In date-range mode, meta.previous and meta.next contain a matching meeting timestamp before from or after to, or null. They are omitted in directional mode. Use include=attendances to add person-level attendance states.

ParameterTypOrtPflichtBeschreibung
group_idintimpl DisplayPfadjaID of group
is_canceledboolQueryFilter by the exact cancellation flag: true selects canceled meetings, false selects non-canceled meetings.
is_completedboolQueryFilter by the exact completion flag.
from_fromstrStringQueryLower inclusive range boundary, or exclusive anchor when direction is supplied.
tostrStringQueryExclusive upper range boundary.
directionstrStringQueryEnable directional paging strictly before or after from; omit for an unpaginated date range.
limitinti64QueryNumber of meetings per page in directional mode only.
includeList[str]Vec<String>QueryInclude additional information

Update a group meeting

Updates meeting timing, completion, cancellation and feedback. Requires authentication, permission to view the group and permission to manage its meetings. Use a meetingId belonging to the group in the URL.

Supply startDate, isCompleted and isCanceled; they have no implicit request defaults. Omitted numGuests, comment and pollResult are cleared to null. This is not a partial update. Change filters have precedence rather than being combined: new_role_id overrides new_status, which overrides new_fields/has_field_changed. PUT/groups/{groupId}/members/{personId}

client.groups.members.update()client.groups().members().update()

Add a person to a group

Creates a membership for the person identified in the path. Both creation and legacy updating return 200. Requires permission to view group members and add members; updating an existing membership additionally checks changed membership properties and custom-field security levels. Set only_add=true to reject existing memberships. Updating through PUT is deprecated in the backend; use PATCH for partial changes. The legacy update path clears omitted comments and end dates but preserves omitted status, role, start date and waiting-list position. Creation checks group capacity unless ignoreGroupFull is true; waiting-list capacity has a separate override. Changes update history, trigger membership events and recalculate the growth path. The response includes a legacy duplicate under data["0"] and a top-level deprecation mapping; use the regular data properties.

Resend pending newsletter confirmation emails

Sends ChurchTools confirmation emails again for eligible pending newsletter-person records in this mapping. Requires visibility of the group and members plus the global churchgroup permission "administer groups". Selecting one recipient with person_id additionally requires visibility of that person. Candidates must have an active membership, a non-archived person, no successful synchronization, no unsubscribe date and no confirmed double opt-in. Add a direct parent-group relationship

Adds parentGroupId as a direct parent of groupId. Groups can have multiple parents; this adds an edge rather than replacing existing parents, and does not copy memberships. Requires global group administration or hierarchy/group editing permission for both groups. Self-parenting and a relationship that would create a cycle are rejected with 400. Get all roles for this group

Returns the roles configured for one group, including inactive roles. Each entry combines a shared role definition from the group's type with settings specific to this group, such as chat access, check-in QR codes and participant capacity. id is the group-specific role settings ID used by PATCH /groups/{groupId}/roles/{roleId}. groupTypeRoleId links to the shared definition from GET /group/roles; do not interchange these IDs. isActive describes whether the role is enabled in this group, not the membership status of any person. PATCH/groups/{groupId}/roles/{roleId}*

client.groups.roles.patch()client.groups().roles().patch()

Update role settings for a group

Updates settings for one role in one group. Use the entry's id from GET /groups/{groupId}/roles as roleId, not its groupTypeRoleId. This does not rename or reclassify the shared role definition. Send only the settings to change. Omitted fields are preserved. growPathId=null clears the growth-path association; htmlTemplateIds=[] clears the template list. A supplied template list replaces the previous list. The default role cannot be deactivated. Returns the complete updated GroupRole in data, without meta. Requires authentication and permission to view the group. Chat settings require one of administer groups, edit group, edit groups of grouptype or +admin group chat for this group. The other role settings except htmlTemplateIds require one of administer groups, edit group or edit groups of grouptype. Adding document templates requires one of administer groups, edit group, edit groups of grouptype or +edit group basic settings, plus the churchcore permission use church html templates for each added template. Templates must belong to the group-membership document domain.

List wiki categories and recent pages from the current group role

POST/publicgroups/{groupId}/signout*

client.publicgroups.signout()client.publicgroups().signout()

Withdraw group registrations

Withdraws selected memberships for the requester or people registered by that requester. A group sign-up token identifies the requester without requiring a login; without a token the current user and group sign-up access are used. When registration is open, active, requested and waiting memberships are eligible. Otherwise the requester needs the group exit permission and only active memberships qualify. All person IDs are checked before changes begin. With automatic acceptance enabled, memberships are deleted; otherwise they are marked to_delete for approval and their role is cleared. The changes run in a transaction. An empty personIds list is a successful no-op. This signs people out of a group, not out of their ChurchTools session.

POST/publicgroups/{groupId}/signup*

client.publicgroups.submit_signup()client.publicgroups().submit_signup()

Submit group signup forms

Submits one form per person using a signup token for this group. Copy field type/id from the dynamic form and use its mandatory/options rules. Existing person IDs must be eligible for this requester; new spouse/child/other forms are available only when allowed by group settings. Adding related/other persons requires hasAcceptedPrivacyForOther=true. A child must be younger than 16. Membership may be accepted immediately, requested from leaders or placed on a waiting list; capacity is checked for the entire submitted set. Depending on group configuration, a new applicant may produce a request email instead of a new person. The operation is transactional for database changes. Success returns a top-level nullable groupHomepageHash, without a data wrapper.

List appointment occurrences across calendars

Returns calculated occurrences for the requested date range, with one entry per occurrence rather than per series. POST/calendars/{calendarId}/appointments/{appointmentId}*

client.calendars.appointments.split()client.calendars().appointments().split()

Split and update an appointment series

Creates a new stored appointment from the supplied complete data and removes the selected scope from the original. splitUntilEnd=true cuts the original off before splitDate and requires a split after the original start. false excludes only splitDate and allows splitting the first occurrence. The returned data.id belongs to the new appointment. The new recurrence must describe the intended replacement; splitting does not automatically restrict it to one date. Linked resources are adjusted by their respective workflows.

GET/events

client.events.list()client.events().list()mit Filtern: .list_with(&GetEventsQuery)seitenweise

Get all events

Returns events visible through calendar permissions or the current user’s valid service assignments. Date comparisons use midnight in the application time zone: to includes exactly midnight, not later events that day. Results from calendar access are merged with events where the user is assigned and deduplicated; this merged range list is not guaranteed to be globally sorted. With direction, selects one page relative to from and ignores to.

ParameterTypOrtPflichtBeschreibung
from_fromdateNaiveDateQueryMidnight anchor or beginning of the range.
todateNaiveDateQueryRange upper bound at midnight, inclusive.
directionstrStringQueryEnable directional pagination; omit for an unpaginated date range.
limitinti64QueryResults per page in directional mode; ignored in range mode.
canceledboolQueryInclude cancelled events in addition to active events.
includestrStringQueryComma-separated Fractal includes.

Rückgabe Paginator[Event]Vec<Event>

for event in client.events.list():
    print(event.name)
for event in client.events().list()? {
    println!("{}", event.name);
}

GET/events/{serviceId}/possiblepersonsforservice

client.events.list_possiblepersonsforservice()client.events().list_possiblepersonsforservice()

Get all possible persons for a service

Returns an unpaginated, deduplicated list of persons from active, non-hidden memberships in groups connected to the service. If connected tags exist, a matching tag is also required. Archived or deceased persons are excluded and hidden-person visibility is respected. With no connected groups, the result is empty.

ParameterTypOrtPflichtBeschreibung
service_idintimpl DisplayPfadjaID of a reusable service role from /services

Rückgabe List[ServiceCandidate]Vec<ServiceCandidate>

for possiblepersonsforservice in client.events.list_possiblepersonsforservice(2):
    print(possiblepersonsforservice.full_name)
for possiblepersonsforservice in client.events().list_possiblepersonsforservice(2)? {
    println!("{}", possiblepersonsforservice.full_name);
}

GET/events/{eventId}

client.events.get()client.events().get()

Get a single event

Returns the event visible to the current user, including calendar, eventFiles and eventServices. Service assignments are filtered by service-group visibility or own assignment; persons can be concealed. The eventServices property is present even when empty. Cancelled events can also be read if visible.

ParameterTypOrtPflichtBeschreibung
event_idintimpl DisplayPfadjaID of Event

Rückgabe EventReadWithServices

event = client.events.get(42)
print(event.name)
let event = client.events().get(42)?;
println!("{}", event.name);

GET/events/ical

client.events.get_ical()client.events().get_ical()Query: GetEventsIcalQuery

Get iCal roster link

Returns the personal roster subscription as JSON. If no secret exists, this GET creates one; otherwise it preserves the existing link. Use meta.iCalUrl to fetch the actual iCalendar feed. A roster contains the person's service assignments at events, including pending requests and confirmed assignments.

person_idinti64QueryjaID of person

    person_id: Some(42),
    ..Default::default()
};

println!("{}", ical.attribute);

PUT/events/{eventId}*

client.events.update()client.events().update()

Update event details

Updates the description, administrators and cancellation state for this service-planning event. It does not update service assignments or the calendar appointment. Changing the administrator set additionally requires the "edit masterdata" permission for the service planning domain; other changes require event administration access, the "edit events" permission for the event calendar, or a corresponding internal group permission.

ParameterTypOrtPflichtBeschreibung
event_idintimpl DisplayPfadjaID of Event
admin_ids"adminIds"List[int]Vec<i64>BodyReplace the administrator list.
description"description"Optional[str]Option<String>BodyEvent description.
event_admin_ids"eventAdminIds"List[int]Vec<i64>BodyLegacy input alias for adminIds.
is_canceled"isCanceled"boolBodyWhether the service-planning event is cancelled.
note"note"Optional[str]Option<String>BodyDeprecated alias for description.

Rückgabe EventDetailsUpdateResult

result = client.events.update(
    42,
    description="Sound check starts 30 minutes before the gathering.",

Send an email to selected event recipients

Sends an email to selected people in the context of one or more events. ChurchTools filters service participants by visible service groups and other selected recipients by person visibility. subject"subject"strStringBodyjaEmail subject.
append_agenda_button"appendAgendaButton"boolBodyjaAppend links for supplied events that have an agenda and for whose calendar the sender has "view agenda" permission.

Accept a service exchange request

Accepts the exchange and swaps the persons assigned to the two event-service assignments, confirming both assignments. The workflow archives the accepted exchange and other active exchanges from the same source assignment, and sends notifications. Requires personId to identify the current user and the person assigned to the requested assignment. Returns the updated exchange request without enriching events or persons.

ParameterTypOrtPflichtBeschreibung
person_idintimpl DisplayPfadjaID of person
request_idintimpl DisplayPfadjaID of a service exchange request

Rückgabe ServiceExchangeRequest

result = client.persons.exchangerequests.update(42, 42)
print(result.id)
let result = client.persons().exchangerequests().update(42, 42)?;
println!("{}", result.id);

DELETE/persons/{personId}/exchangerequests/{requestId}*

client.persons.exchangerequests.delete()client.persons().exchangerequests().delete()

Decline a service exchange request

Declines the exchange by setting its status to DECLINED and sending a notification. The request remains stored and its archive flag is unchanged; the assignments are not swapped. Requires personId to identify the current user and the person assigned to the requested assignment. Returns the updated exchange request without enriching events or persons. Already answered requests are returned unchanged.

ParameterTypOrtPflichtBeschreibung
person_idintimpl DisplayPfadjaID of person
request_idintimpl DisplayPfadjaID of a service exchange request

Rückgabe ServiceExchangeRequest

exchangerequest = client.persons.exchangerequests.delete(42, 42)
print(exchangerequest.id)
let exchangerequest = client.persons().exchangerequests().delete(42, 42)?;
println!("{}", exchangerequest.id);

POST/agendas/send*

client.agendas.send()client.agendas().send()veraltet

Send agenda email to recipients

Deprecated compatibility endpoint for POST /events/send. Recipients are filtered to selected participants in visible service groups or other selected people the sender may view and the response reports the effective scope. sendCopyToMe can add the sender. Events do not have to share an agenda. Agenda links are included for events whose agenda the sender may view.

ParameterTypOrtPflichtBeschreibung
body"body"strStringBodyjaHTML email body. ChurchTools appends buttons for all supplied events and any requested, available agenda and file links.
event_ids"eventIds"List[int]Vec<i64>BodyjaEvents used to resolve participating recipients and message links.
recipients"recipients"List[int]Vec<i64>BodyjaSelected person IDs. Only selected participants in visible service groups of the loaded events, or selected people the sender may otherwise view, receive the message.
send_copy_to_me"sendCopyToMe"boolBodyAlso include the currently logged-in person as a recipient, even if their ID is absent from recipients.
subject"subject"strStringBodyjaEmail subject.
append_agenda_button"appendAgendaButton"boolBodyAppend links for supplied events that have an agenda and for whose calendar the sender has "view agenda" permission.
files"files"List[int]Vec<i64>BodyFile IDs to list as links in the message body.

Export event agenda

Generates a presenter import archive for an event agenda. Requires a super administrator, an event administrator, "view agenda" or "edit agenda" for the event calendar, or involvement in the event. client.events.agenda.integrate()client.events().agenda().integrate()Query: PostEventsIdAgendaIntegrateQuery

Integrate agenda with another event

Links the target event in the path to the existing agenda of the source event given by event_id. This creates a shared agenda, not a copy: item IDs, content and lock state are shared with all already linked events. Event dates remain independent and item times are calculated per event. Hidden-item settings of the source event are not copied to the new link. Requires agenda editing permission for the target and agenda viewing permission for the source.

GET/songs

client.songs.list()client.songs().list()mit Filtern: .list_with(&GetSongsQuery)seitenweise

Get all songs

Returns songs in categories for which the caller has view songcategory or edit songcategory permission. Songs are sorted by name, then ID, both ascending. Filters are combined with AND; query matches either title or author. Category filters are intersected with permitted categories. No permitted or matching songs returns an empty list. Each song includes all arrangements, including those that do not match key_of_arrangement. Results are paginated.

ParameterTypOrtPflichtBeschreibung
song_category_idsList[int]Vec<i64>QueryRestrict to these song category IDs, intersected with permitted categories.
idsList[int]Vec<i64>QueryRestrict to these song IDs.
practiceboolQueryFilter the rehearsal flag: true selects songs marked for practice, false selects those not marked.
key_of_arrangementstrStringQueryFilter by arrangement key.
namestrStringQuerySubstring filter on the song title, combined with query and the other filters.
querystrStringQuerySubstring search in either title or author, combined with name and the other filters.
includeList[str]Vec<String>QueryOptional enrichments.
limitinti64QueryNumber of songs per page, from 1 to 200.

POST/songs/{songId}/arrangements/{arrangementId}/files/{fileId}/transpose*

client.songs.arrangements.files.transpose()client.songs().arrangements().files().transpose()

Create a transposed arrangement audio file

Transposes an existing audio file by one to six semitones and saves a new file on the arrangement identified by arrangementId. The original file is retained. Processing is synchronous, so the response is sent after conversion and saving finish. Pitch is changed with tempo compensation to preserve the playback duration. The output retains the source filename extension and contains audio only. Supported formats depend on the server's FFmpeg installation; an unsupported or unreadable input causes an error. Each successful call creates a new file record. This does not update the arrangement's key or tempo metadata. Requires view permission for churchservice and edit permission for the source file; for song arrangement files, this is edit songcategory permission for the source song's category.

ParameterTypOrtPflichtBeschreibung
song_idintimpl DisplayPfadjaID of song
arrangement_idintimpl DisplayPfadjaID of arrangement
file_idintimpl DisplayPfadjaID of the file
transpose_interval"transpose-interval"strStringBodyjaPitch shift in semitones: up1 through up6 raise the pitch by one to six semitones, down1 through down6 lower it.

client.bookings.list()client.bookings().list()Query: GetBookingsQuery

List booking occurrences

Returns occurrences overlapping the requested date range for the selected resources. The same recurring booking ID can appear more than once with different booking.calculated dates. from and to are inclusive local dates. Requires permission to view every selected resource. Booking details may be anonymized.

todateNaiveDateQueryLast included local date, on or after from.

GET/groups/{groupId}/absences

client.groups.list_absences()client.groups().list_absences()mit Filtern: .list_absences_with(&GetGroupsAbsencesQuery)

Fetch all absences for persons in a group

Returns absences for active, visible group members. Requires access to the group; member results are additionally restricted by manage absent or the internal group permission to view absences. Returns absences whose start is at or before to and whose end is at or after from. Absences ending exactly at midnight on the from date are also included, even if from specifies a later time that day. Dates use the application time zone; UTC timestamps are converted into it. Without filters the window starts at midnight two weeks ago and ends at midnight two weeks from today. The list is unpaginated and sorted by start; meta.count is the number returned.

toUnion[date, datetime]serde_json::ValueQueryEnd of the overlap window.
order_directionstrStringQueryOrder by absence start.
from_dateUnion[date, datetime]serde_json::ValueQueryLegacy alias for from.
to_dateUnion[date, datetime]serde_json::ValueQueryLegacy alias for to.

GET/wiki/pages

client.wiki.list_pages()client.wiki().list_pages()mit Filtern: .list_pages_with(&GetWikiPagesQuery)seitenweise

List wiki pages

Lists the latest revisions of non-system, non-redirect pages in viewable categories. Guest category permissions are supported. Omitted/empty wiki_category_ids selects every viewable category; inaccessible IDs are silently dropped. Without query, ordering defaults to display title, then GUID. With query, default ranking prefers matching category main pages, then title matches, exact-content matches and finally matches containing all query words. Explicit order_fields overrides ranking. Pagination is applied after finding and enriching all matching pages. Text is omitted unless include[]=text; include[]=preview returns an unrendered stored-text prefix, which may contain raw HTML. searchPreview is independently included when query is supplied. meta contains page count and pagination total/limit/current/lastPage; lastPage is 0 for no results.

ParameterTypOrtPflichtBeschreibung
limitinti64QueryMaximum page size.
querystrStringQueryTrimmed search term. SQL LIKE wildcard characters % and _ are interpreted by the backend.
wiki_category_idsList[int]Vec<i64>QueryWiki category IDs that should be included.
order_fieldsList[str]Vec<String>QueryFields used to sort the result.
order_directionsList[str]Vec<String>QuerySort directions matching order_fields[] by position.
includeList[str]Vec<String>Querytext returns Markdown or sanitized HTML; preview returns a raw stored-text prefix without HTML sanitization.
preview_lengthinti64QueryMaximum number of characters returned in textPreview when include[]=preview is requested.

Rückgabe Paginator[SimpleWikiPage]Vec<SimpleWikiPage>

for page in client.wiki.list_pages():
    print(page.title)
for page in client.wiki().list_pages()? {
    println!("{}", page.title);
}

GET/wiki/search

client.wiki.list_search()client.wiki().list_search()Query: GetWikiSearchQuery

Full-text search across wiki pages

Searches latest non-system, non-redirect pages in categories the current user or guest can view. Omitted/empty wiki_category_ids means all viewable categories; inaccessible categories are silently dropped. Results are grouped by relevance: category-name main pages, title matches (shorter first), exact text matches and then matches containing all query words. Results are deduplicated by GUID and are not paginated. The query is not trimmed; SQL LIKE wildcard characters % and _ are interpreted. Results contain domain-object links and a text preview with Markdown emphasis for matches, not the full page. For paginated page resources, use GET /wiki/pages.

ParameterTypOrtPflichtBeschreibung
querystrStringQueryjaSearch term. Must contain at least one character.
wiki_category_idsList[int]Vec<i64>QueryWiki categories that should be searched.

Rückgabe List[WikiSearchResult]Vec<WikiSearchResult>

for search in client.wiki.list_search(query="welcome"):
    print(search.title)
let query = GetWikiSearchQuery {
    query: Some("welcome".into()),
    ..Default::default()
};
for search in client.wiki().list_search(&query)? {
    println!("{}", search.title);
}

GET/wiki/categories

client.wiki.categories.list()client.wiki().categories().list()

Get all wiki categories

Lists wiki categories for which the current user (including a guest) has churchwiki view category permission. Categories organize pages and define their access permissions. Results are sorted by sortKey, then stored name, without pagination. inMenu does not filter this catalog. Each category’s canEdit/canDelete flags describe page operations based on edit category, not permission to rename or delete the category itself. The top-level permissions.editMasterData flag controls category administration. meta.count counts visible categories.

Rückgabe List[WikiCategory]Vec<WikiCategory>

for category in client.wiki.categories.list():
    print(category.name)
for category in client.wiki().categories().list()? {
    println!("{}", category.name);
}

POST/wiki/categories

client.wiki.categories.create()client.wiki().categories().create()

Create a new wiki category

Creates a wiki category and an initial page titled main (version 1, empty text, Markdown enabled). Requires churchwiki edit masterdata. The creator receives view category and edit category permissions for the new category if missing. A nonexistent campusId silently resolves to null. The returned category has an empty permissions object; use the list to obtain page-operation hints.

ParameterTypOrtPflichtBeschreibung
campus_id"campusId"Optional[int]Option<i64>BodyOptional campus association.
file_access_without_permission"fileAccessWithoutPermission"boolBodyjaWhether files in this wiki category can be read without category-view permission.
in_menu"inMenu"boolBodyjaWhether the category should appear in navigation menus; it is still returned by the category catalog when false.
name"name"strStringBodyjaCategory name; unlike page titles it is not trimmed.
sort_key"sortKey"inti64BodyjaSort order; negative values are accepted.

Get a wiki page

Requires churchwiki view category permission, including any permissions assigned to guests. For a protected system page in category 0, super-administrator access also permits the individual read. Returns one page revision with text: Markdown is returned as stored, legacy HTML is sanitized, and null content becomes an empty string. Prefer the stable page GUID; legacy titles are accepted and Unicode ellipsis characters in titles are normalized to three periods. PATCH/wiki/categories/{wikiCategoryId}/pages/{identifier}

client.wiki.categories.pages.patch()client.wiki().categories().pages().patch()

Update a wiki page

Updates only supplied text, isMarkdown and onStartpage fields on the latest revision identified by GUID. Titles cannot be changed through this endpoint. Requires category edit permission; protected system pages in category 0 require a super administrator. Changed text creates the next revision with the same GUID; unchanged text or changes only to the flags modify the existing latest revision. Trimmed blank/null text clears the stored content. No expected-version or ETag precondition is accepted, so this endpoint does not provide optimistic edit-conflict protection.

ParameterTypOrtPflichtBeschreibung
wiki_category_idintimpl DisplayPfadjaID of WikiCategory
identifierstrimpl DisplayPfadjaGUID of the wiki page.
is_markdown"isMarkdown"boolBody
on_startpage"onStartpage"boolBody
text"text"Optional[str]Option<String>BodyTrimmed replacement content.

}))?;

POST/checkin/persons*

client.checkin.create_persons()client.checkin().create_persons()mit Filtern: .create_persons_with(&PostCheckinPersonsQuery)

Create new person and add to group

Creates a person and admits them to a group for the check-in workflow. Requires administer persons, or create person in churchcheckin plus group meeting permission and a person security level covering the selected status. Masterdata IDs are installation-specific. Ordinary duplicate-person confirmation is bypassed; a unique GUID and license limits still apply. A creation note and optional tag are saved before the membership. This request does not record meeting attendance or print a label; perform the actual check-in separately. Failure can leave earlier steps saved because the whole workflow is not one transaction. The response is the legacy person model, not the regular Person representation.

ParameterTypOrtPflichtBeschreibung
without_privacy_policy_agreementboolQueryOmits the otherwise mandatory privacy policy agreement fields.
group"group"CheckinMembershipCreateBodyjaMembership to create before a separate attendance check-in.
person"person"CheckinPersonDataCreateBodyjaPerson fields for creation during check-in admission.
tag_id"tagId"Optional[int]Option<i64>BodyOptional person-tag ID.

)
print(result.first_name)

client.checkin.update_persons()client.checkin().update_persons()

Put existing person into group

Admits an existing person to a group using its default role and check-in membership origin, optionally adds a tag, and updates person fields configured for that group. Requires administer persons or group meeting permission. Existing membership is a conflict, not an idempotent success. The operation does not record attendance or print labels. Tag changes occur before membership creation and can remain after a failed request. The returned legacy person-model representation differs from the regular Person API.

GET/followups

client.followups.list()client.followups().list()mit Filtern: .list_with(&GetFollowupsQuery)seitenweise

List follow-ups assigned to the current user or eligible groups

Returns follow-ups owned by the current user plus unassigned group follow-ups for groups where the user has follow-up execution or administration rights. This includes personal and membership follow-ups; it is not an unrestricted list of every follow-up for a visible person. Archived subject persons are excluded. Date filters use effectiveDueDate and are combined with OR. Results are sorted by doneDate descending, then effectiveDueDate ascending, then ID ascending; finished items can precede open ones. Page/limit slice the result, but meta only contains count for this page, without a total or last page.

ParameterTypOrtPflichtBeschreibung
filterList[str]Vec<String>QueryRepeat to select any of the listed states.

Get follow-up

Returns one follow-up, including its subject person/group context, responsible person, current/original due dates and configured completion group. The current owner may view it; a group-associated follow-up is also visible to users with that group’s follow-up execution or administration rights. This direct check is broader than the list selection: group follow-ups assigned to another person can be read by eligible group staff even when omitted from their list. The response does not include notes or history, nor indicate whether its underlying specification is shared.

DELETE/followups/{followUpId}

client.followups.delete()client.followups().delete()

Delete follow-up

Deletes the follow-up and records deletion history in a transaction. Its specification is also deleted when it is not shared; a shared specification remains. Deletion requires access to the subject person and, for a group-associated follow-up, follow-up administration rights in that group. No dryRun/dependency-preview behavior is implemented. This removes the follow-up rather than marking it finished; it does not reverse group memberships or routine effects caused by earlier completion.

ParameterTypOrtPflichtBeschreibung
follow_up_idintimpl DisplayPfadjaID of Follow-up

Rückgabe None()

POST/followups/{followUpId}/complete

client.followups.complete()client.followups().complete()

Complete follow-up

Sets doneDate to the current timestamp and records completion history. The subject person must be visible. Group-associated follow-ups require "churchdb +do followup" permission in that group. A supplied nonzero successGroupId adds or updates the subject’s membership in that selected group, including overwriting an existing membership’s role/status. Configured fixed-group/group-type restrictions are checked; a configured group is not selected automatically. Emits a completion event, which can trigger configured continuations or routines. Repeating this operation replaces doneDate, writes another history entry and emits another event. Due dates are retained.

ParameterTypOrtPflichtBeschreibung
follow_up_idintimpl DisplayPfadjaID of Follow-up
success_group_id"successGroupId"Optional[int]Option<i64>BodySelected destination group.

Rückgabe FollowUp2

    "successGroupId": 42
}))?;
let followup = client.followups().complete(2, &body)?;
println!("{}", followup.title);

POST/followups/{followUpId}/dismiss

client.followups.dismiss()client.followups().dismiss()

Dismiss follow-up

Marks the follow-up as finished by setting doneDate to the current timestamp and recording a dismissal history entry. The subject person must be visible. Group-associated follow-ups require "churchdb +do followup" permission in that group. No success-group membership is changed and no completion event is emitted. Completion and dismissal both appear through doneDate and differ only in history. Repeating dismissal updates doneDate and creates another history entry.
